answers.justification: For the approved cohort A investigator-assessed PFS interim result (29 March 2019; randomized abemaciclib+NSAI vs placebo+NSAI), the article reports ITT and 119 events, 66/207 vs 53/99, with median follow-up about 16 months (eh_97a4618cbe20d154); event counts and ITT membership do not establish how many participants had observed/censored PFS data or the missing-outcome extent. Treatment discontinuation is reported but follow-up after stopping is not established here. Thus neither near-complete nor materially incomplete outcome availability is demonstrated.
unknowns: Arm-specific PFS outcome availability/censoring counts and reasons at the cutoff; whether outcome ascertainment continued after treatment discontinuation.

limitations.premise: The extent of observed PFS outcome data for all randomized participants remains unknown.
limitations.stopping_rationale: Inspected the main article and all supplement pages; the participant-flow figure extraction did not yield readable flow counts, the bounded source search failed integrity verification, and retained registry bytes are unavailable. No replacement or network retrieval was attempted.

answers.justification: The available inspected reporting gives the primary ITT analysis and event results but no bias-correcting or missing-outcome sensitivity analysis (eh_40041818a00a52ba; eh_97a4618cbe20d154). This is not evidence that bias occurred; it does not show the result was unbiased.
unknowns: Whether an unobserved-outcome sensitivity analysis was conducted elsewhere; whether missing outcomes biased the estimate.

limitations.premise: No retrieved evidence demonstrates that the approved estimate was unbiased by missing outcome data.
limitations.stopping_rationale: Only captured local material was used; search projection integrity failed and registry raw bytes were unavailable.

answers.justification: Neither reasons for loss/censoring nor their relationship to true PFS outcome are reported in the inspected passages. Treatment discontinuation, including discontinuation commonly due to progression (eh_97a4618cbe20d154), does not establish loss of outcome follow-up or the mechanism.
unknowns: Reasons/timing for PFS censoring or loss to follow-up and whether related to health/outcome.

limitations.premise: Whether missingness could depend on true PFS remains unresolved.
limitations.stopping_rationale: No cause-specific censoring or loss-to-follow-up accounting was recovered in the inspected local Sources.

answers.justification: The inspected evidence does not quantify differential missingness/censoring or provide reasons permitting assessment of likely outcome dependence. The reported event proportions are not missingness proportions.
unknowns: Differential censoring/missingness and its causes across randomized groups.

limitations.premise: Likelihood that missingness depended on true PFS cannot be assessed.
limitations.stopping_rationale: Captured-source retrieval was bounded; the historical registry projection was unavailable and not replaced.
